advances: An exact family of compatible interval and full-dimensional box witnesses for a particular midpoint-density centroid selector. The normalized actual upper bounds are at the selected point, and a separate reflected point is safe.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The endpoint midpoint body is $D=(A+C)/2=[(1-a)/2,1]\times Q$, contained in $B$, with volume $s=(1+a)/2$. At a point of the lifted hull with base zero the two endpoint weights must be equal. Grouping them gives a convex combination of a point of $D$ and one of $B$, so the middle fiber is exact. The other two integer bases are extreme. The hull is full-dimensional because it contains full-dimensional fibers at distinct bases. Its three volumes are $a,1,1$, each strictly below $(2+a)/2$. In particular $|\,|B|-|C|\,|=0<a$ and $|B|\ge s_d$, the latter because convexity of the $d$th power gives $s_d\le(1+a)/2\le1$.

The affine map $(x_1,x')\mapsto(k+(x_1-k)/a,x')$ sends uniform probability on $A$ onto uniform probability on $C$. Its midpoint map sends uniform probability on $A$ to uniform probability on $D$. Scaling the joint probability by $a$ gives $\eta=(a/s)\mathbf1_D\,dx$. Since $s_d\le s$, this gives the claimed density bound. When $d=1$, $s=s_d$ and any midpoint measure with the same marginals satisfying that bound has support in $D$ and must attain the density bound almost everywhere on $D$ to have mass $a$.

The first coordinate of the midpoint mean is $k$ for any coupling because both endpoint centroids have first coordinate $k$. The transverse means are all $1/2$. The full-target measure has mass $2+a$ and first moment $1/2+(1+a)k$, giving the displayed $g_a$. It satisfies
$$
g_a-\frac{1-a}{2}=\frac{1+4a+a^2}{4(2+a)}>0,\qquad
1-g_a=\frac{3+2a+a^2}{4(2+a)}>0.
$$
Thus $(0,g)$ is an actual point and the middle cap is properly cut. At base $-1$ its threshold $g_a-1<0$ is below $\min A_1=3(1-a)/4$. At base $1$ its threshold is $g_a+1>\max C_1$ because $g_a-(1-a)/4=(3+3a)/(4(2+a))>0$. Consequently the actual raw mass is $1-g_a+a$, which gives the displayed normalized formula. Its middle trace captures a length $1-g_a$ in both $B$ and $D$. This gives the auxiliary formula, and the actual mass exceeds that cost by $a-(a/s)(1-g_a)>0$, because the trace misses a positive-volume part of $D$.

At $(d,a)=(1,1/10)$ one has $s_d=s=11/20$, $\eta$ has density $2/11$ on $D$, $g_a=173/280$, the target is $21/40$, the auxiliary cost is $1391/3080$ and the actual mass is $27/56$. Subtraction gives the stated deficits and slack. At $(d,a)=(2,1/100)$ one has $s_d=121/400<s=101/200$, density $2/101<4/121=a/s_d$, $g_a=16733/26800$ and $\mu(H)=2067/5360$. The normalized mass is $3445/17956$, and $2/9-3445/17956=4907/161604>0$. The auxiliary cost is strictly smaller than the original mass here as well.
statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $0<a<1$, $Q=[0,1]^{d-1}$ and $k=(3-a)/4$. For $d=1$ the transverse box is a point with unit counting mass. Take fibers
$$
A=[k-a/2,k+a/2]\times Q,\quad B=[0,1]\times Q,\quad
C=[k-1/2,k+1/2]\times Q
$$
at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull, with total mixed volume $M=2+a$. These are its exact positive integer fibers, each smaller than $M/2$. Put $s_d=((a^{1/d}+1)/2)^d$. The mass-$a$ midpoint measure $\eta$ of an explicit uniform-marginal coupling has density $(2a/(1+a))\mathbf1_{(A+C)/2}$ bounded above by $(a/s_d)\mathbf1_B$. This upper bound on the density coefficient is attained for $d=1$.

The centroid $g$ of $\mathbf1_B\,dx+[(1+a)/a]\eta$ is independent of the uniform-marginal coupling. Its first coordinate is $g_a=(5+2a-a^2)/(4(2+a))$ and all others are $1/2$. At the closed ambient halfspace $H=\{(z,x):x_1-z\ge g_a\}$ through $(0,g)$ with middle trace $H_0$, the normalized original mass and the raw auxiliary cost are
$$
\frac{\mu(H)}M=\frac{5a^2+10a+3}{4(2+a)^2},\qquad
|B\cap H_0|+\eta(H_0)=(1-g_a)(1+2a/(1+a)).
$$
Writing $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, both the original cap mass and the auxiliary cost are strictly below $\Gamma_dM/2$ for $(d,a)=(1,1/10)$ and $(2,1/100)$. In dimension one the deficits are $3/70$ and $113/1540$ respectively, and the actual endpoint pairing slack is $47/1540$. In dimension two the normalized actual deficit is $4907/161604$.
title: An actual box family for failure of the full-target midpoint-density centroid
